# AlphaForgeBench: Benchmarking End-to-End Trading Strategy Design with Large Language Models

arXiv [2602.18481](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.18481) · v1 2026-02-10 · latest 2026-05-27

> **Machine-extracted method card.** The gloss column was written by `claude-opus-5-5` (effort medium) on 2026-10-23 from the html text of the paper. "Not found" means the model did not find the item in the text it was given, not that the paper omits it.

| Field | Gloss | Quote from the paper |
|---|---|---|
| **task** | Benchmarking LLMs as quantitative researchers that generate executable alpha factors and factor-based trading strategy code, rather than emitting buy/hold/sell actions directly. | “Rather than requiring models to emit discrete trading actions, AlphaForgeBench tasks LLMs with generating executable alpha factors and composing factor-based trading strategies grounded in financial domain knowledge.” |
| **architecture** | A generate-and-backtest pipeline. A standardized prompt combines a system instruction, the strategy query and a factor library. The LLM returns a Python generate_signal function, which a deterministic backtest engine executes. Queries come from real-world extraction (via gemini-3-flash-preview) plus LLM-augmented 3x3 difficulty queries. | “The model must return a self-contained Python function (generate_signal) that consumes a dataframe of OHLCV columns and precomputed indicator factors and produces a trading-signal series dictating position actions (e.g., invest versus hold cash).” |
| **data** | Daily OHLCV with precomputed technical indicators for 7 assets: BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT from Binance; AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, NVDA and TSLA from Yahoo Finance. Queries: 633 real-world single-asset queries plus 270 structured queries. | “Each generated strategy is executed within the unified backtest engine across 7 assets spanning two distinct market regimes: 2 cryptocurrencies (BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT; sourced from Binance) and 5 US equities (AAPL, GOOGL, MSFT, NVDA, TSLA; sourced from Yahoo Finance).” |
| **window** | 5-year evaluation window from 2021-01-01 to 2026-01-01, with a 300-day lookback; no train/validation split is described. A separate direct-trading instability study used BTC over 01/01/2025–01/01/2026. | “The evaluation window spans 5 years (2021-01-01 to 2026-01-01), deliberately selected to cover heterogeneous market conditions including bull rallies, bear corrections, AI-driven recoveries, and prolonged consolidation phases” |
| **models** | claude-sonnet-4.5, deepseek-v3.2, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3-pro-preview, gpt-5.2 and grok-4.1-fast, all via official APIs. gemini-3-flash-preview was used for extraction and gpt-5.2 for query generation. | “We benchmark six frontier LLMs spanning five providers: claude-sonnet-4.5, deepseek-v3.2, gemini-3-flash-preview, gemini-3-pro-preview, gpt-5.2, and grok-4.1-fast.” |
| **baselines** | The LLMs are compared against each other, and the code-generation paradigm is compared against direct-trading (action-emitting) LLM setups. | “The results confirm that AlphaForgeBench offers a significantly more stable and discriminatory assessment of financial capabilities compared to direct-trading baselines.” |
| **headline_result** | On real-world queries over 2021–2026, gemini-3-pro-preview is best: SR 0.449±0.262, ARR 0.171±0.123, MDD 0.174, CR 1.411, SoR 0.767, VOL 0.237. On structured queries it reaches SR 0.628 at T=0. | “\| gemini-3-pro-preview \| 0.449 \pm 0.262 \| 0.171 \pm 0.123 \| 0.174 \pm 0.119 \| 1.411 \pm 1.165 \| 0.767 \pm 0.493 \| 0.237 \pm 0.162” |
| **costs** | Main text uses a fixed one-way transaction cost of 10^{-3} with no slippage or liquidity modeling. Appendix Table 9 instead lists a transaction cost of 0 (frictionless), so the paper is inconsistent. Inference cost is not quantified. | “and a fixed one-way transaction cost of 10^{-3} , thereby isolating intrinsic signal quality from confounding portfolio-construction effects.” |
| **uncertainty** | k=5 independent generations per query, with metrics reported as mean ± std. A temperature ablation compares τ=0 and τ=0.7. Intra-query std is reported as an order of magnitude below inter-query std, and figures show 25th–75th percentile bands. | “Every experiment runs k{=}5 independent generations per query to quantify run-to-run variability.” |
| **leakage_controls** | Only for the direct-trading instability study, the most recent window (2025–2026) was chosen to minimize training-data leakage. No contamination control is described for the main 2021–2026 benchmark. | “Notably, we choose the window 01/01/2025–01/01/2026 to minimize data leakage. Some models may have been trained on market data from earlier periods, which would introduce leakage risk; we therefore use the most recent available span.” |
| **limitations** | Scope is limited to single-asset, long-only strategies with a fixed cost and no slippage or liquidity modeling. Results measure strategy design quality, not deployable performance. Stage 2 queries are augmentations rather than broad ecological coverage. | “The current evaluation targets single asset long only strategy design under a standardized backtesting environment with a fixed transaction cost of 10^{-3} and without explicit slippage or liquidity modeling.” |
| **release** | Code and data (query set, pipeline, backtest engine, scripts) are promised publicly upon acceptance. A webpage is at https://finbrain-lab-hkustgz.github.io/AlphaForgeBench. | “All code and data will be publicly available upon acceptance of this paper, including the benchmark query set, evaluation pipeline, backtest engine, and supplementary scripts for reproducing the reported results.” |
